status.label: Handled by the DLL-corruption installation tracking issues
status.detail: A maintainer explicitly grouped this report with #32525 and #42181; new comments add user/system-install comparison but do not create a distinct fix scope.

next_action.label: Keep the report linked to the existing installation investigation
next_action.reason: Starting a separate implementation would duplicate the maintainer's tracking issues and the existing WinUI3Apps deployment investigation.

judgment.rationale: The maintainer's April 2026 tracking comment explicitly groups this issue with #32525 and #42181 as DLL file errors during install or upgrade. Later reports reproduce the same class of failure on PowerToys 0.100.1 and distinguish user-setup from system-wide behavior, but do not establish a separate root cause or fix scope.
evidence: The original report describes an auto-update from PowerToys 0.85.1 that failed with multiple missing or unloadable WinUI3Apps DLLs.
A maintainer comment titled 'Tracking: DLL/Corruption Installation Errors' links #32525 and #42181 and says all three issues concern DLL file errors during installation or upgrade.
Issue #32525 is closed as not planned and explicitly cross-references #35949; issue #42181 is also closed as not planned and cross-references #35949.
A June 2026 commenter reproduced the failure after relaunch or wake from sleep on PowerToys 0.100.1.
A September 2026 commenter reports that reinstalling the user setup still produced corrupt DLL errors while the system-wide installer worked, adding scope information but no confirmed fix.
No assignee, linked pull request, or issue-specific implementation attempt is present for #35949.
judgment.recommended_action: Do not start parallel code work for #35949. Retain the user-versus-system-install observation as evidence on the existing DLL-corruption installation tracking issue(s) and let maintainers decide whether to reopen or split the scope.

fix_assessment.rationale: The issue is already handled as part of the maintainer's DLL-corruption installation tracking. A separate PowerToys code fix cannot be justified from this report without duplicating the linked investigation; no existing PR is claimed as a resolution.

issue_context.summary: An upgrade or relaunch can leave WinUI3Apps DLLs missing or unloadable. Maintainers explicitly track this report with the broader installation-corruption issues, while recent commenters add evidence that user and system installers may behave differently.
known_information: The issue is open and labeled Issue-Bug, Area-Setup/Install, and Needs-Triage.
The original report concerns an automatic upgrade from PowerToys 0.85.1 and multiple DLL load failures.
A commenter resolved one older occurrence by using the installer Repair option.
A maintainer's public tracking comment links #32525 and #42181 and states that all three reports concern DLL file errors during install or upgrade.
Issue #32525 and #42181 are closed as not planned and both cross-reference #35949.
A June 2026 report says the issue can occur after wake from sleep, update checking, or closing and relaunching PowerToys 0.100.1.
A September 2026 report says reinstalling the user setup still failed while the system-wide installer worked.

Current source includes installer WinUI3Apps component generation in installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/WinUI3Applications.wxs, Quick Accent launch of WinUI3Apps\PowerToys.PowerAccent.exe in src/modules/poweraccent/PowerAccentModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp, and installation verification entries in tools/Verification scripts/verify-installation-script.ps1.
inferences: The user-versus-system-install difference may identify an installer scope, file-lock, or repair-path distinction, but it does not prove that the PowerAccent DLL is the source of the broader corruption.
The relaunch and wake-from-sleep reports suggest that file deployment and process/lifecycle state may interact, but no public log identifies the failing installer transaction.
Because the maintainer already consolidated the issue family, any new implementation plan should be created only on the tracking issue after maintainers choose the shared fix scope.
issue_context.analysis: The public tracking comment and timeline provide stronger ownership evidence than the old artifact's blank-assignee inference. Current source confirms that WinUI3Apps files are generated as installer components and that Quick Accent and the verification tooling depend on that deployment, but the issue spans multiple DLLs and installation paths. The proper triage result is handled elsewhere, preserving the recent user/system-install distinction without creating duplicate agent work.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and all four public comments, including the maintainer tracking comment and the newest user-versus-system-install report.
Checked the issue timeline: #32525 and #42181 cross-reference #35949; the maintainer comment groups the reports as DLL/corruption installation errors.
Reviewed installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/WinUI3Applications.wxs, which defines the WinUI3Apps install component group and generated file-component insertion point.

Reviewed src/modules/poweraccent/PowerAccentModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp, where Quick Accent launches WinUI3Apps\PowerToys.PowerAccent.exe, and tools/Verification scripts/verify-installation-script.ps1, which verifies the PowerAccent WinUI3Apps files.
Reviewed related issue states: #32525 and #42181 are closed as not planned; no open or merged PR is linked as a fix for #35949.

Searched installation/DLL-related issue activity and found the same corruption/install family, but no confirmed duplicate outside the maintainer-linked tracking issues and no issue-specific fix attempt.
